title: Technical Details
text: observed biomarker measurements modeled : V_{ij}=m_i(T_{ij})+\varepsilon_{ij},\quad =1,\ldots,n,\quad j=1,\ldots,n_i : V_{ij}: Observed biomarker value subject time T_{ij} m_i(t): True underlying biomarker trajectory \varepsilon_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{e}^{2}): Measurement error evolution biomarker trajectories governed second-order linear differential equation, captures dynamic behavior system: \ddot{m}_i(t) + 2 \xi_i \omega_i \dot{m}_i(t) + \omega_i^2 m_i(t) = k \omega_i^2 \mu_i(t), \xi_i denotes damping ratio, \omega_i represents natural frequency, k serves scaling parameter, \mu_i(t) characterizes external input function driving system. accommodate subject-specific heterogeneity covariate effects, reformulate differential equation using linear mixed-effects approach: \ddot{m}_{}(t) = (\beta_{m} + b_{,m}) m_{}(t) + (\beta_{\dot{m}} + b_{,\dot{m}}) \dot{m}_{}(t) + (\boldsymbol{\beta}_{X} + \mathbf{b}_{,X})^{\top} \mathbf{X}_i(t), \boldsymbol{\beta} = (\beta_{m}, \beta_{\dot{m}}, \boldsymbol{\beta}_{X}^{\top})^{\top} fixed effects, \mathbf{b}_i = (b_{,m}, b_{,\dot{m}}, \mathbf{b}_{,X}^{\top})^{\top} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b) random effects, \mathbf{X}_i(t) covariates. parameters connect standard form via: \beta_{m} + b_{,m} = -\omega_i^2, \quad \beta_{\dot{m}} + b_{,\dot{m}} = -2\xi_i\omega_i, \quad (\boldsymbol{\beta}_{X} + \mathbf{b}_{,X})^{\top} \mathbf{X}_i(t) = k\omega_i^2\mu_i(t) yielding subject-specific dynamics: natural frequency \omega_i = \sqrt{-(\beta_{m} + b_{,m})}, damping ratio \xi_i = -\frac{\beta_{\dot{m}} + b_{,\dot{m}}}{2\omega_i}, external forcing k\mu_i(t) = \frac{(\boldsymbol{\beta}_{X} + \mathbf{b}_{,X})^{\top} \mathbf{X}_i(t)}{\omega_i^2}.

title: Technical Details
text: hazard function incorporates biomarker dynamics: \lambda_i(t) = \lambda_{0}(t)\exp\left[\alpha_1 m_i(t) + \alpha_2 \dot{m}_i^{\gamma}(t) + \mathbf{W}_i(t)^{\top}\boldsymbol{\phi}\right] : \lambda_{0}(t): Baseline hazard function \mathbf{W}_i(t): Covariate vector (time-dependent time-independent) regression coefficients \boldsymbol{\phi} \gamma \\{0, 1, 2\}: Power parameter velocity contribution, \gamma = 0 corresponds velocity effect (.e., \alpha_2 term excluded), \gamma = 1 yields linear velocity effect \alpha_2\dot{m}_i(t), \gamma = 2 yields quadratic velocity effect \alpha_2[\dot{m}_i(t)]^2

title: Technical Details
text: complete system couples biomarker trajectory dynamics survival process. state vector \mathbf{s}_i(t) = (\Lambda_i(t), m_i(t), \dot{m}_i(t))^{\top} evolves according : \frac{d\mathbf{s}_i}{dt} = \begin{pmatrix} \lambda_i(t) \\ \dot{m}_i(t) \\ \ddot{m}_i(t) \end{pmatrix} initial conditions \mathbf{s}_i(0) = (0, m_{i0}, \dot{m}_{i0})^{\top}, m_{i0} \dot{m}_{i0} initial biomarker value velocity subject .

title: Technical Details
text: parameter estimation, specify following parametric forms: Survival Hazard: log baseline hazard modeled flexibly using B-splines: \log\lambda_0(t) = \boldsymbol{\eta}^{\top} \mathbf{B}^{(\lambda)}(t) \mathbf{B}^{(\lambda)}(t) = [B_1^{(\lambda)}(t), \ldots, B_q^{(\lambda)}(t)]^{\top} B-spline basis q basis functions, \boldsymbol{\eta} \\mathbb{R}^q corresponding coefficients. \lambda_i(t) = \exp\left[\boldsymbol{\eta}^{\top} \mathbf{B}^{(\lambda)}(t) + \alpha_1 m_i(t) + \alpha_2 \dot{m}_i^{\gamma}(t) + \mathbf{W}_i(t)^{\top}\boldsymbol{\phi}\right] Trajectory Dynamics: computational convenience, express differential equation compact matrix form: \ddot{m}_{}(t) = \mathbf{Z}_i(t)^{\top}(\boldsymbol{\beta} + \mathbf{b}_i) \mathbf{Z}_i(t) = [m_{}(t), \dot{m}_{}(t), \mathbf{X}_i(t)^{\top}]^{\top} combines state variables covariates.

title: Technical Details
text: model contains continuous random effects \mathbf{b}_i \\mathbb{R}^p latent variables, necessitating use Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm maximum likelihood estimation. marginal likelihood subject obtained integrating unobserved random effects: L_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \int p(\mathbf{V}_i | \mathbf{b}_i) \cdot p(T_i, \delta_i | \mathbf{b}_i) \cdot p(\mathbf{b}_i) \, d\mathbf{b}_i \boldsymbol{\theta} = (\boldsymbol{\beta}, \boldsymbol{\eta}, \boldsymbol{\phi}, \alpha_1, \alpha_2, \gamma, \sigma_e^2, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b) includes model parameters, following likelihood components: \begin{aligned} \text{Longitudinal:} \quad & p(\mathbf{V}_i | \mathbf{b}_i) = \prod_{j=1}^{n_i} \mathcal{N}(V_{ij}; m_{}(T_{ij}|\mathbf{b}_i), \sigma_e^2) = (2\pi\sigma_e^2)^{-n_i/2} \exp\left[-\frac{1}{2\sigma_e^2}\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}[V_{ij} - m_{}(T_{ij}|\mathbf{b}_i)]^2\right]\\ \text{Survival:} \quad & p(T_i, \delta_i | \mathbf{b}_i) = [\lambda_{}(T_i|\mathbf{b}_i)]^{\delta_i} \exp[-\Lambda_{}(T_i|\mathbf{b}_i)]\\ \text{Random Effects:} \quad & p(\mathbf{b}_i) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b) = (2\pi)^{-p/2}|\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b|^{-1/2}\exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b^{-1}\mathbf{b}_i\right] \end{aligned} m_{}(t|\mathbf{b}_i) denotes trajectory solution random effects \mathbf{b}_i, p = \dim(\mathbf{b}_i) dimension random effects.

title: Technical Details
text: subject , apply AGHQ approximate p(\mathbf{b}_i | \mathcal{O}_i, \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}) \mathcal{O}_i = \{\mathbf{V}_i, T_i, \delta_i\}. joint log-density : \begin{aligned} \log p(\mathcal{O}_i, \mathbf{b}_i) &= -\frac{n_i}{2}\log(2\pi\sigma_e^2) - \frac{1}{2\sigma_e^2}\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}[V_{ij} - m_{}(T_{ij}|\mathbf{b}_i)]^2 \\ &\quad + \delta_i\log\lambda_{}(T_i|\mathbf{b}_i) - \Lambda_{}(T_i|\mathbf{b}_i) \\ &\quad - \frac{p}{2}\log(2\pi) - \frac{1}{2}\log|\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b| - \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b^{-1}\mathbf{b}_i \end{aligned} AGHQ procedure: Find mode: \hat{\mathbf{b}}_i = \arg\max_{\mathbf{b}_i} \log p(\mathcal{O}_i, \mathbf{b}_i) Compute Hessian: \mathbf{H}_i = -\nabla^2 \log p(\mathcal{O}_i, \mathbf{b}_i)\big|_{\mathbf{b}_i = \hat{\mathbf{b}}_i} Cholesky decomposition: \mathbf{H}_i^{-1} = \mathbf{L}_i \mathbf{L}_i^{\top} AGHQ marginal likelihood : \tilde{p}(\mathcal{O}_i) = |\mathbf{L}_i| \sum_{k=1}^{K} \omega_k p(\mathcal{O}_i, \mathbf{L}_i \mathbf{x}_k + \hat{\mathbf{b}}_i) AGHQ posterior density : \tilde{p}(\mathbf{b}_i | \mathcal{O}_i) = \frac{p(\mathcal{O}_i, \mathbf{b}_i)}{\tilde{p}(\mathcal{O}_i)}

title: Technical Details
text: Q-function Q(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \sum_{=1}^n \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{b}_i | \mathcal{O}_i, \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}}[\ell_i(\mathbf{b}_i; \boldsymbol{\theta})] \ell_i(\mathbf{b}; \boldsymbol{\theta}) = \log p(\mathcal{O}_i, \mathbf{b} | \boldsymbol{\theta}). Using AGHQ posterior approximation nodes \mathbf{b}_{ik} = \mathbf{L}_i \mathbf{x}_k + \hat{\mathbf{b}}_i: Q(\boldsymbol{\theta}) \approx \sum_{=1}^n |\mathbf{L}_i| \sum_{k=1}^{K} \omega_k \ell_i(\mathbf{b}_{ik}; \boldsymbol{\theta}) \tilde{p}(\mathbf{b}_{ik} | \mathcal{O}_i, \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}) Since AGHQ posterior normalized, define weights \tilde{w}_{ik} = |\mathbf{L}_i| \omega_k \tilde{p}(\mathbf{b}_{ik} | \mathcal{O}_i, \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)}). Using definitions: \tilde{p}(\mathbf{b}_{ik} | \mathcal{O}_i) = \frac{p(\mathcal{O}_i, \mathbf{b}_{ik})}{\tilde{p}(\mathcal{O}_i)}, \quad \tilde{p}(\mathcal{O}_i) = |\mathbf{L}_i| \sum_{j=1}^{K} \omega_j p(\mathcal{O}_i, \mathbf{b}_{ij}) obtain: \tilde{w}_{ik} = \frac{\omega_k \exp[\ell_i(\mathbf{b}_{ik}; \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})]}{\sum_{j=1}^{K} \omega_j \exp[\ell_i(\mathbf{b}_{ij}; \boldsymbol{\theta}^{(t)})]} Jacobian cancels. Thus: \boxed{Q(\boldsymbol{\theta}) \approx \sum_{=1}^n \sum_{k=1}^{K} \tilde{w}_{ik} \ell_i(\mathbf{b}_{ik}; \boldsymbol{\theta})} : \begin{aligned} \ell_i(\mathbf{b}_{ik}; \boldsymbol{\theta}) &= -\frac{n_i}{2}\log(2\pi\sigma_e^2) - \frac{1}{2\sigma_e^2}\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}[V_{ij} - m_{}(T_{ij}|\mathbf{b}_{ik})]^2 \\ &\quad + \delta_i\log\lambda_{}(T_i|\mathbf{b}_{ik}) - \Lambda_{}(T_i|\mathbf{b}_{ik}) \\ &\quad - \frac{p}{2}\log(2\pi) - \frac{1}{2}\log|\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b| - \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}_{ik}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b^{-1}\mathbf{b}_{ik} \end{aligned} Parameter updates: Maximize Q(\boldsymbol{\theta}) via L-BFGS-B. Variance components closed-form updates: \boxed{\sigma_e^2 = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{=1}^n \sum_{k=1}^{K} \tilde{w}_{ik} \sum_{j=1}^{n_i} [V_{ij} - m_{}(T_{ij}|\mathbf{b}_{ik})]^2} \boxed{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{=1}^n \left[\hat{\mathbf{b}}_i\hat{\mathbf{b}}_i^{\top} + \hat{\mathbf{V}}_i\right]} N = \sum_{=1}^n n_i \tilde{w}_{ik} subject-specific normalized weights.

title: Joint Modeling of Longitudinal and Survival Data Using ODEs
text: Longitudinal Model: Biomarker trajectories evolve according second-order ODE: \ddot{m}_i(t) + 2 \xi_i \omega_i \dot{m}_i(t) + \omega_i^2 m_i(t) = k \omega_i^2 \mu_i(t) m_i(t) biomarker value, \dot{m}_i(t) velocity (rate change), \ddot{m}_i(t) acceleration. Subject-specific dynamics characterized natural frequency \omega_i damping ratio \xi_i, \mu_i(t) representing external forcing (e.g., treatment effects, covariates). Individual heterogeneity captured random effects ODE parameters. Survival Model: hazard function incorporates biomarker dynamics: \lambda_i(t) = \lambda_{0}(t)\exp\left[\alpha_1 m_i(t) + \alpha_2 \dot{m}_i^{\gamma}(t) + \mathbf{W}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{\phi}\right] \gamma \\{0, 1, 2\} controls velocity power (0: velocity, 1: linear, 2: quadratic).

text: biomarker trajectory \(m_i(t)\) subject \(\) follows damped harmonic oscillator external forcing: $$\ddot{m}_i(t) + 2\xi\omega\dot{m}_i(t) + \omega^2 m_i(t) =   k \omega^2 [f_0 + \mathbf{X}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta}_{exc}]$$ : \(\omega = 2\pi/T\) natural angular frequency \(\xi\) damping ratio determining oscillation behavior \(k\) scales excitation amplitude \(f_0\) constant excitation term \(\mathbf{X}_i\) contains time-invariant covariates \(\boldsymbol{\beta}_{exc}\) represents covariate effects excitation Initial conditions specified : \(m_i(0) = \mu_{m,0} +     \mathbf{X}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta}_{m,init}\) \(\dot{m}_i(0) = \mu_{v,0} +     \mathbf{X}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta}_{v,init}\) observed longitudinal measurements incorporate additive Gaussian noise: $$y_{ij} = m_i(t_{ij}) + b_i + \epsilon_{ij}$$ \(\epsilon_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_\epsilon^2)\) represents independent measurement error.

Visualize patient-specific dynamics distribution library(ggplot2)  # Recover original xi and period from dynamics parameters mu <- attr(sim_full$random_effects, "mu") dynamics_df <- as.data.frame(sim_full$random_effects) dynamics_df$omega <- sqrt(-dynamics_df$dyn_value - mu["dyn_value"]) dynamics_df$xi_implied <- -(dynamics_df$dyn_slope + mu["dyn_slope"]) /   (2 * dynamics_df$omega) dynamics_df$period_implied <- 2 * pi / dynamics_df$omega  # Distribution of damping ratios ggplot(dynamics_df, aes(x = xi_implied)) +   geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +   geom_vline(xintercept = 0.4, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +   labs(title = "Distribution of Patient Damping Ratios",        x = "Damping Ratio (xi)", y = "Count") +   theme_minimal()   # Joint distribution of xi and period ggplot(dynamics_df, aes(x = period_implied, y = xi_implied)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +   geom_density_2d(color = "steelblue") +   labs(title = "Patient-Specific Dynamics",        x = "Period", y = "Damping Ratio (xi)") +   theme_minimal()   # Compare trajectories for patients with different dynamics # Select patients at 10th, 50th, 90th percentiles of xi quantiles <- quantile(dynamics_df$xi_implied, probs = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9)) example_ids <- sapply(quantiles, function(q) {   which.min(abs(dynamics_df$xi_implied - q)) })  plot_data <- sim_full$longitudinal_data[   sim_full$longitudinal_data$id %in% example_ids, ] plot_data$xi_group <- factor(   plot_data$id,   levels = example_ids,   labels = c("Low xi (10%)", "Median xi (50%)", "High xi (90%)") )  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = time, y = biomarker, color = xi_group)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   labs(title = "Biomarker Trajectories by Damping Ratio",        x = "Time", y = "Biomarker Value",        color = "Patient Group") +   theme_minimal()   #
